reviews.text: 可以说是超出预期的一个塔防游戏，可惜只有无尽模式，如果未来能更新故事模式就好了 另外有个建议，希望能设置单个塔默认攻击最前方的敌人或者血量最低的敌人等，气球塔防里就有类似的设计，我觉得让塔更智能一些会玩得舒服很多。
这个游戏可以说有点王国保卫战的影子，接近于传统类型的塔防游戏，整体质量非常不错，尤其是地块拼合的玩法属于开创了自己的赛道，然后配合于轻肉鸽的玩法，让可玩性更是上了一个台阶，上头程度呈指数上升，总而言之，这款游戏未来可期。

I've already spent some 100 hours playing the demo for this. It's still a little rough around the edges, but the concept - building the hexagonal-tiled lands that you need to defend - is really compelling and fun in its simplicity.

1500+ Games and DLC and this is my first ever negative review. Ouch. I do reserve the right to change this up but a strategy game that works SO HARD against you and so hard against any real strategy is simply, not fun. Needs heavy balancing to be done (and if the game features multiple levels of difficulty, the easiest should be a calm intro-type experience). A difficult game that makes some sense, great. A game that is difficult simply to frustrate? Not my thing. However, I do get that for many that is EXACTLY what they want, and if thats you, this is a solid game for sure. Looks great. Sounds great. Tough for no other reason than to be tough.

延伸道路，堵死入口，建设塔防，守卫城堡，《六方守护者》是一款集运营策略、轻度肉鸽、地图拼接于一体的塔防游戏，白天布置塔防，夜晚抵御入侵，敌人每波都会通过随机一个或多个入口发起入侵，并随着波次强化血量；玩家通过六边形的地图拼接、不断搭建防御纵深、创造有利地形，并依靠兵营与防御塔的互相搭配、抵御敌人的入侵。 [h1] 六边形的地图拼接[/h1] 《六方守护者》作为一款塔防游戏，其塔防核心玩法方面，最重要的创新与趣味就在六边形的地图拼接玩法。玩家需要通过击杀敌人获取地块素材，用于抽取随机地块，并通过六边形的地图拼接，构建起蜿蜒曲折的道路、从而改变敌人的入口位置与进攻路线，为防守布置带来便利与策略性。 新置入的板块，必须和地图上已有的道路、水路能够相接，这种策略性布局的“卡卡颂“拼接+六边形的可旋转地形也让我想起了另一款有趣的休闲建造类游戏《筑梦颂》，而本作也和《筑梦颂》一般，上手十分容易，但考虑起来也同样硬核~ [h1] 能够堵死入口的开放式塔防[/h1] 整体这种能够操控、影响敌人的入口与前进道路的开放式塔防设计，我个人玩过的有《变量》、《重构》这两款，就直观体验而言，地图拼接方式与各自差异化的肉鸽元素，这三款的游戏塔防风格还是各有不同的~其中最主要的不同我认为在于，本作的敌人入口数量可以由玩家通过地块连接来进行改变。 一般而言，这种开放式塔防的主要策略性，在于延长线路带来更多的塔防布置空间、敌人更长前进时间，并通过路线规划，使得敌人能够较长时间停留在我方布置的火力集中区域。 而本作则还融入了敌人入口多少的变化！玩家能够利用稀有的死路地板，或者依靠合理规划道路的首尾环形相连，来堵死敌人的某些入口。当在战斗中堵死入口，可以直接挤死传送门内剩余未入场的敌人，而长远来看，减少入口也降低了多线作战所带来的困难。 不过如果留存的入口数量过少，也会导致剩余的入侵敌人被激怒，从而最大血量、攻击上升，因此也需要做出一定抉择与判断。 [h1] 肉鸽方面：每天选择新的塔[/h1] 至于，塔防游戏最重要的塔防方面，虽说一些具体塔防元素比较传统，有塔有兵、塔能升级，但实际体验大相径庭，本作采用的并非很多塔防游戏的关卡制形式，而是采用了生存形式+肉鸽模式、坚守尽可能多天数的玩法。 游戏包括防御塔、兵营、生产建筑、奇观等多种类型以及法术，玩家能够布置的建筑/法术也并非开局选择，是在游戏内随天数不断获取，每天获取一个新的建筑，或使某种类的已有建筑获得整体强化；还具有“祝福”这一通过消耗特殊资源或击败精英获取的全局强化。 整体的难度在于敌人每天都会通过随机一个或多个入口、在夜晚发起入侵，其中昼夜之分、时间机制并不考察手速与思考速度，因为随时可以暂停；主要的困难在于敌人会随着波次强化血量，而单一建筑，建造与升级都会越建越贵，因此对于建筑的选择、金钱花销的投入也需要一定的规划与安排，从而使得游戏硬核并需要多次尝试。 [h1] 塔防生存形式的重复挑战[/h1] 目前具有5种地图类型+2种构筑挑战模式，每张地图还具有3种难度。每张地图也带来不同的特性与特殊地形，比如沙漠图的特殊地形绿洲，比如高地的高地能够增加防御塔范围，有的地图也会直接附带一个主动法术。 整体通过肉鸽带来的随机性，游戏的每局塔防布置与策略抉择中都有不同的体验，也依靠每局挑战积累的金币，升级解锁更多防御塔与永久性强化内容，使得玩家能够不断尝试新的策略与方法进行游玩。 [h1]总结[/h1] 相较于一众出入口固定的塔防游戏，带有随机性与额外策略性的地形拼接玩法+轻度肉鸽元素的防御塔获取，使得游戏具有较高的可重玩性。整体画面清新，上手容易，轻松耐玩，能带来足够的趣味，感兴趣的可以入手尝试。 [quote]加入[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/GHYX]干货游戏[/url]&关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35106417/]咱的鉴赏家[/url]，不定期为大家带来游戏体验分享，也期待您来一起分享自己的游戏体验干货~[/quote]
这游戏的更新频率很快。 ------------------------- 之前有提过一些问题，甚至作者还给我进行了回复，这让我很惊讶，说明作者是真的有想把游戏做的让大家都喜欢的，而且最近更新也确实在一个一个的改平衡。 不过我还是觉得，要是给选择地块和选择卡牌的地方加个刷新键游戏体验会更好哈哈哈，也希望这个游戏能越来越好。
完了两个多小时了，已经把所有地图的简单都玩到10天以上。先说优点，自己可以改变地图的这点很好玩。然后全是缺点，敌人成长太离谱了，12天的时候3级塔打几乎不掉血；经济系统不够平衡，防御塔在10天的时候也只能造几个，根本不够；过于看脸了，改变地形消掉出兵口看脸，每天的随机升级看脸，卡池里面垃圾一堆看脸。看看后续更新吧，如果能改的话还是可以推荐的。

还不错，内容量已经值会票价了。虽然是EA，但完成度相当高，教程把所有的系统讲的很清楚，还可以锁定内容，防止解锁过多导致污染牌库，UI也很舒服。 游戏有着卡卡颂的内核，地块拼接完美贯穿整个游戏进程。很多拼地块的塔防游戏在大后期路太长而磨磨唧唧，或者毫无影响，拼接最后成了一种折磨。而这游戏可以通过拼出死胡同来关闭出怪口，不需要的地块可以放在边角丢掉，最终以关闭所有出怪口为目标并获得奖励分。拼接从前期到后期都是相当重要的，是塔防和拼图的完美结合。 让我有点难受的是开局随机的地形太关键了……有的开局随便就能关掉几个传送门，而水陆交错的开局要费好大劲，希望开局的水陆交错能多给点房子作为奖励……

Let's be clear. This game is great for what it is. I'm feeling a particular need to chime in here because 1) it isn't getting a lot of traction and 2) The negative reviews are unusually brain dead. Straight away let's address the "rougelite" tag. It's word that draws people in like crack or keeps them away like the plague. There are random elements that materially affect the game and create varied play throughs, but it doesn't scratch that same itch for me. The randomness feels like the cure for tower defense games. No crutch relying on the same build path every game. It's less rouge like and more shifting ground you're constantly trying to adapt to. Really clever. Past that, Hexgaurdian is a very fancy Carcassone. The tiles are just as important as anything else and your ability to think highly strategically and plan ahead determines their effective. Not RNG. Which isn't to say that you can't get unlucky, but it seems to me that people are chasing an ideal tile placement rather than properly staggering the spawns in one direction. I made it to wave 30 on my fourth play through; I have some authority here. The economic options are also interesting. Repeated use of a tower and its upgrades scale across all towers and upgrades. Its yet another way of the game naturally enforcing diversity. Given this, the game should probably offer more towers early on so early runs aren't choked out without counter play, but going forward it creates a unique relationship between build and money that I don't think I've seen before. Wayyy better than the rougelite tower defenses I've seen before. By like, a lot. I'm never this purely reactionary, but I'm just going to respond to some of the nonsense directly now: - You can save in game and come back. It's literally right there if you pause. -The meta progression is visually a bit of a mess to look at but not problematic. In terms of grind, it's objectively better than Bloons. Why are you morons citing the worst meta progression perhaps in the history of video games? I knocked out 25% of the progression in this game in a single good run; sucks to suck. -On that note, why is Bloons even in this conversation. Outside of being tower defense, there is no other comparison. Completely different niches. Completely different ways that you engage with the mechanics. It's bizarre to me seeing such a fun void capturing people like it has. How dare TD not be the exactly same over and over and over and over. -Towers are boring? Yeah, little bit. You unlock some more interesting options going through but the overall visuals and visual progressions are pretty bland (and even a little hard to discern the difference between a lv 1 and lv 3 tower at a glance). For $10, I'm not particularly upset about what are probably stock assets, or at least made by one guy who visuals aren't their expertise. SUMMARY Great tower defense with a focus on varied play through and forcing some trying strategic decisions. If you can't figure out how to play with the tiles, it's going to be a very hard game for you, but the tiles are the best part of the entire game.It's on the cusp of being a really great game. For the price, I'm happy with this as a complete product. If there are updates, all the better. As is, Hexguardian is reaching towards greatness without quite hitting the right beats to make it there. It's very very good. To the Dev-- who seems to be active in these reviews-- maybe change the artwork. It looks like a child's Duplo set. 7/10

TLDR: This is a fun take on the Tower Defense genre, but it's hamstrung by major performance issues that make the mid-game to late-game literally unplayable. Can't recommend until this is addressed. The performance issues are the only reason I'm giving this a negative review. Having played enough to unlock some of the better turret/unit options, I got a run to survive past 40 days...and then realized I'd hit a hard wall because the game starts slowing to a crawl at that point. By day 46 I was getting single-digit FPS, and I decided to let myself die there just to end it. It kills any motivation to continue unlocking new powerups and buildings when the game performance itself won't allow me to make proper use of them. I was defeated not by endlessly scaling enemies, but by the game unable to process it all. Optimization should be the dev's primary focus in my opinion. It may also help to implement some graphics options, because right now all we can do is choose resolution and fullscreen/windowed. The main gimmick of creating your map via adding new hex-tiles is incredibly fun for a tower-defense game. You can completely shut off the spawning of some enemy types by closing off entry portals for them (and even win a game by closing them ALL)...but this can also be punishing at times if you're not careful. The game has a "rage" mechanic that does percentage buffs for enemies based on how many portals they're expecting to come through versus what you'd made available on your map. This can make closing off pathways backfire on you, because the enemies that do come through your chokepoints may now have the sheer health and armor to break through. This creates an interesting dynamic of trying to make longer tracks of land and turrets to whittle down enemies while also closing off spawn portals that are too close, WHILE ALSO avoiding closing too many portals at once. That said, the tiles you get are completely random, so you can get massively screwed over by RNG...either by not being able to close off unfavorable portals, or by being given strings of "garbage" tiles that may just make your map harder to defend. You currently purchase a random tile via in-game currency gathered from defeated enemies. I would like to see a more expensive option to buy a specific tile type (even if its gated behind progression or something), or maybe even a boss/mini-boss killing reward that grants a single tile of your choice. It's not a game breaking issue, but I think players might appreciate late-game rewards of having more options to mitigate the RNG involved in this. Progression in the game comes from getting "trophies" from playing runs, with you getting more for surviving longer. With those trophies, you can unlock new turrets/units, new passive buffs, resource generation buildings, etc. It's well implemented and provides a lot of incentive to keep playing.

The creators clearly played RogueTower and thought, "I like it but it needs polish." And they definitely polished it, but that is all they did. They made it shiny but didn't really fix any problems. Some they made worse. Most of all, the reason why I do not like RogueTower, and by extension this game, is the way the RNG is handled. The RNG doesn't seem like it would be a problem, at the start, but as you get deeper in, the RNG becomes a bigger and big problem. The biggest offender is the card system for unlocks, that happen in between levels. You could be doing well in the run when suddenly you need 1 specific tower unlocked to complete the level and never see that tower, because the RNG decided that you needed buffs for the tower that is not doing the element/effect you now need. And you would think that with more towers you unlocked the better things would be. But nope. As you unlock more things all you are really doing is clogging the the RNG cards. Need a new tower to deal more damage? Well here is a buff that doesn't really help, a support building, and new wonder unlock. At least with RogueTower you could increase the number of cards you could choose from and increase the number of cards you could get over time to offset the increased number of things in the RNG wheel. Then there is the expanding out of the lanes. I do not know how they managed it, but somehow they made lane expansion feel even more chaotic and RNG based than in RogueTower. Like the only thing you got to choose, in RogueTower, was which direction to expand and somehow it feels like I had more choice there than here in Hexguardian. And I hope you love multi-lanes. Cause you don't have any choice. Every map starts with at least 6 lanes and you will never know which lane the enemies are coming out of next time. Sure you know which ones they come out this time and you build all your towers on that lane to be able to actually hold things, and then BAM! Tons of enemies on the neglected lane. And god forbid you actually try to make things more manageable by closing lanes. Close too many and suddenly the enemies gain massive buffs. Need to close that one lane because you cannot afford to put enough towers on that one random lane in the middle of nowhere because the RNG tiles decided, F@#% you, this game? Too bad, either lose to that one lane or lose to super buffed enemies. All of this isn't helped by the strangely large tile sizes and tiny tower ranges. You would think that surely with the reposition-able units you could cover a larger area than with the static towers. But you would be wrong. Due to the way lane/tile expansion works, you will never be able to sufficiently cover the massive expanse of the map. And have enough damage. Half of which is buried in the talent tree. Making each run more of a I just need to grind more games, THEN, I can have the damage to progress. Which leads into the biggest problem the game has, your skill doesn't really matter. You will only succeed or fail based on the RNG you are given. You can go in with the best laid plan, but if RNG doesn't give you something even moderately helpful, or worse, only gives you stuff that hurts; you are doomed.

To be honest, I only have one beef with this game. It hits a lot of the buttons that Rogue Tower hits, but in a much more attractive package. If you like tower defense but want to be able to alter the board, this is a great pick-up. The beef? The unit AI is super spotty. I like having NPCs on the road to intercept, but watching them can be infuriating. When a bad guy aggroes a good guy, the bad guy just stands still on the road while the good guy puts out his cigarette, calmly puts a bookmark in the book he was reading, sighs heavily, then saunters over to the waiting NPC so they can start fighting. Ranged NPCs are just as bad - they're about as motivated as a 16 year old working on prom night. Otherwise, this game's pretty good. Plenty of unlocks (even tho the unlock page could use.... SOMETHING. It's really, really busy), plenty of tile types, a few modes. It's good stuff.

The idea is nice, has lots of potential but something about this game just turns me off. :/ From the slight sluggishness of the UI / handling to the art that is not 100% to my liking, I just don't really enjoy my time with it. 6/10 First time playing a roguelite Tower defense game. It is very cool how you build your own map as you play. You can even close of paths completely. Reducing the amount of enemies you get, and give you more control. How ever, whilst this is a cool concept, the rng is way to heavy. Almost everything is dependent on rng. What Towers you will be able to use, what upgrades you will get and the map pieces. Some issues here. 1) The economy is terrible. Towers and upgrades does not have a set price, they will instead get more expensive each time you buy one. Very quickly will you struggle for money, The worst part about it is that the upgrades that you buy is worse than the ones you can get for free after each round. Most buyable upgrade is just a big blast radious, 2 extra foot soldiers, and some turrets can hit 2 enemies instead of just 1. It sounds good, until you realise that the free upgrades will increase your attack speed, damage, crit chance and damage. cause your turrets to deal and place an elemental attack / effect on hit. These free upgrades offer so much more than the ones you have to buy, so why is the prices so high ? 2) Enrage mechaninc. All enemies will get buffed, Their Health, Armor and Movement speed will be increased. Very quickly will they just run past all of your towers and cause you to lose. When you first start getting to round 10 is nearly if not impossible. Now 11 hours in i am struggling to get to round 20. This buff they get is far to strong and starts way to early. 3) The camera is not the greatest. To zoomed in and if you select a tile to place down, the camera can just freeze up and you will have to move your mouse back and forth until it respons. 4) The talent tree has its prices all over the place. It is not like the price goes up the further down the path you go, it is just random prices. Also for whatever reason, you will only get 80% of your points back if you reset the Talent tree. You will lose a lot to no fault of your own due to it being a rouguelite. It is a cool, unique and kind of fun game, but the Rng and the terrible economy and with how qucikly enemies becomes overpowered. Really really makes it a frustrating ordeal. For the price you will find some enjoyment and i would kind of recomend it. But damn do these cons really bring it down.
